strategy.thesis: Canada's first student-run venture capital fund: scout teams of student investors on 20+ university campuses source and back student-founded startups (at least one founder must be a student) with ~$50K SAFE checks, while training students to become VCs.

application.how_to_apply: Apply online at frontrow.ventures/apply; at least one founder must be a current undergraduate or graduate student.

summary.en: Front Row Ventures is Canada's first student-run venture capital fund, launched in 2017 by Real Ventures. It operates regional micro-funds (Quebec, Ontario, Western Canada) staffed by student investors across 20+ campuses, backing student-founded startups with ~$50K SAFEs. Its CAD$5.5M FRV-CAN-22 fund closed over-subscribed in 2023; over five years it invested in 35+ companies including Valence Discovery (acquired by Recursion).

strategy.thesis: Philanthropically funded, University of Calgary-based venture fund that bridges the gap between innovation demonstration and commercialization, investing $50K–$300K in pre-seed/seed startups connected to the university using a milestone investment methodology; returns are reinvested into the fund.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the UCeed Opportunity Fund application form (University of Calgary / Innovate Calgary); ventures must have a connection to the University of Calgary.

summary.en: UCeed is the largest philanthropically driven, university-based investment fund of its kind in Canada, run via Innovate Calgary at the University of Calgary since 2020. It deploys $50K–$300K into pre-seed/seed startups across six themed funds (Health, Energy, Social Impact, Haskayne Student Fund, Child Health & Wellness, Neuro). It has deployed CAD$8M into 44 startups and holds CAD$22M in AUM.

strategy.thesis: Canada's first student-advised venture capital fund: full-time MBA and Commerce students at Queen's Smith School of Business source deals, conduct due diligence and recommend investments of up to $150K to an Investment Advisory Board of seasoned VCs and angels; deals are syndicated with leading Canadian VCs.

application.how_to_apply: Ventures are sourced and contacted by the student fund team; due diligence runs August–December with recommendations to the Investment Advisory Board in December.

summary.en: Launched in 2006 at Queen's University's Smith School of Business, the TriColour Venture Fund is Canada's first student-advised venture capital fund. Full-time MBA and Commerce students manage a multi-million-dollar (~CAD$3M) fund, investing up to $150,000 per company alongside an Investment Advisory Board of professional investors. Seeded by Queen's alumni, all returns are reinvested.

summary.en: Launched in March 2026, the UBC Catalyst Ventures Fund is a co-investment partnership between the University of British Columbia and InBC Investment Corp. With up to CAD$40M ($10M UBC + $10M InBC + up to $20M private capital), it invests in life sciences and deep tech spinoffs from licensed UBC research and ventures founded by UBC faculty, staff, students and recent alumni. UBC research has spawned 280+ spinoffs generating an estimated $13B in sales.

name.local: ACET Capital (Accélérateur de création d'entreprises technologiques)

strategy.thesis: Venture capital funds attached to the Université de Sherbrooke's technology accelerator (ACET), financing Quebec technology companies at seed/startup stage; capitalized by private investors plus institutional backers (Investissement Québec, National Bank). Quantacet (2023) is described as Canada's first fund reserved exclusively for quantum technology.

application.how_to_apply: Promising companies in the ACET accelerator can obtain equity investment from the associated ACET Capital venture funds; apply via the accelerator at acet.ca.

summary.en: ACET (Accélérateur de création d'entreprises technologiques), founded in 2011 at the Université de Sherbrooke, runs the ACET Capital venture funds (Capital 1 launched 2013; Capital 2 capitalized at CAD$7.6M; Quantacet, launched 2023, billed as Canada's first quantum-only fund). The funds back Quebec seed/startup-stage tech companies, backed by private investors plus Investissement Québec and National Bank.

strategy.thesis: Canada's first university-housed, student-managed social impact fund: Memorial University students deploy capital (micro and general loans) into purpose-driven, social-purpose organizations across Newfoundland and Labrador, with wrap-around investment-readiness and impact-measurement support.

application.how_to_apply: Social-purpose organizations in Newfoundland and Labrador can apply; the fund is housed at Memorial's Centre for Social Enterprise and offers investment-readiness training and impact measurement support.

summary.en: Launched June 2025 at Memorial University's Centre for Social Enterprise, Fairlead is Canada's first university-housed, student-managed social impact fund. Students deploy real capital (micro and general loans, ~CAD$75K) into purpose-driven organizations across Newfoundland and Labrador. It is part of CSE's Impact Investing Fellowship, developed with national nonprofit Propel Impact, and is backed by the Suncor Energy Foundation, the provincial government and private donors.
